title: season
description: The season at block and month scale (#139). A BLOCK is a maximal run of consecutive training weeks closed by an absence of `gap_weeks` or more calendar weeks carrying no load — see ADR 0011. That boundary is used because it is the only one in the data that is not a judgment call: textbook build/recover cycle detection fits 9 of 96 real training weeks, so a detector built on it segments noise. Blocks are DESCRIBED and never named — there is no `base`/`build`/`peak` field, because those are claims about intent and load observes only volume (#154). `slope_tss_per_week` is the regression slope of weekly load across the block and `trend_r2` how much of the week-to-week movement it explains; a low r2 means the block had no trend, which is an answer rather than a gap. Both are withheld (`trend_known: false`) under three weeks, where r2 is 1 by construction. A long block is reported as long and never subdivided — splitting it would fabricate the boundary this definition exists to avoid. `weeks` counts weeks WITH training while `span_weeks` counts the calendar weeks the block covers; they differ wherever a rest week sits inside a block, and `mean_weekly_load` divides by `span_weeks` so it matches the dates. `closed: false` means no absence has ended the block — records simply stop — so its numbers are still moving and a single new session can change them substantially. `end_date` is the last day WITH training, never the end of its calendar week. `sessions` counts activities, matching `months[].sessions`. Polarization uses the same power-else-HR-zone fallback every other stride surface uses, so it agrees with `summary`. `ftp_*` names the sport family it belongs to, because a rowing threshold and a cycling FTP are different quantities and an athlete may have both; the range covers the period and the family with the most sessions in it.
